senses.definition: A high-pitched, short and somewhat sharp sound.
examples: My car used to make an odd ping, but after the last oil change it went away.

quotes.text: With a sudden ping, there was a rabbit there in the black labyrinth with him[.]
quotes.reference: 1982, Douglas Adams, Life, the Universe and Everything, page 89:

senses.definition: (submarine navigation) A pulse of high-pitched or ultrasonic sound whose echoes provide information about nearby objects and vessels.
examples: The submarine sent out a ping and got an echo from a battleship.

senses.definition: (networking) A packet which a remote host is expected to echo, thus indicating its presence.
examples: The network is overloaded from all the pings going out.

senses.definition: (text messaging, Internet) An email or other message sent requesting acknowledgement.
examples: I sent a ping to the insurance company to see if they received our claim.

senses.definition: (video games) A means of highlighting a feature on the game map so that allied players can see it.
To make a high-pitched, short and somewhat sharp sound.
examples: My car was pinging until my last oil change.

quotes.text: The microwave pinged. He forked the steak onto the plate and set the timer again.

senses.definition: (submarine navigation) To emit a signal and then listen for its echo in order to detect objects.
(networking) To send a packet in order to determine whether a host is present, particularly by use of the ping utility.
examples: The server pings its affiliates periodically.

quotes.text: Just because you cannot ping a server or telnet to it does not mean that the server is down or inaccessible.

senses.definition: (by extension) To send an email or other message to someone in hopes of eliciting a response.
examples: I'll ping the insurance company again to see if they've received our claim.

quotes.text: If any deeper etymology is required, Arthur, don't ping me; I'll ping you.
